queries.text: I recommend that you my recommendation is

triggerProbe.absentWhen: The case is not an advised one, so no suitability report is required.

queryGroups.requirement: Client-specific rationale for each recommendation, linked to specified goals

queries.text: I have recommended this because it meets your objective and is in your best interests
this recommendation is suitable for you given your circumstances and what you told me
adviser rationale for the recommendation recorded in the file note or planning notes
one recommendation per existing plan retain switch encash advice given

falsePositiveGuards: Identical rationale bullets repeated verbatim across several recommendations are boilerplate — count them once and mark isClientSpecific false.
A rationale that names the client's actual figures, plans or stated words is client-specific even if the sentence structure is templated.

sufficiency.ifAssertionAbsent: Potential Concern: a recommendation with no stated reason cannot demonstrate suitability.
sufficiency.ifEvidenceAbsent: Note that the rationale is unsupported by any research or meeting record, and weight by how specific the rationale is.

queryGroups.requirement: Justification for the particular product, provider, wrapper and investment

queries.text: why this provider has been recommended platform financial strength service charges
I have recommended a personal pension for the following reasons wrapper choice
why these funds have been selected investment strategy rationale diversification
provider and platform comparison research whole of market panel selection
centralised investment proposition investment committee approved fund list

falsePositiveGuards: A provider's marketing strengths stated in isolation are not a justification for selecting it over alternatives — distinguish absolute claims from comparative ones.
Firm panel or CIP membership is a legitimate justification if the report says so; do not require a fresh whole-of-market search where a documented panel process exists.

sufficiency.ifEvidenceAbsent: Potential Concern where the report asserts a comparison was carried out but no research document exists.

queryGroups.requirement: Personalised language linked to individual circumstances

queries.text: you have told me that you want and this is why the recommendation reflects that
generic explanation of how the product works aims and benefits
specific client preference recorded such as simplicity consolidation adviser involvement

falsePositiveGuards: Standard regulatory wording (tax caveats, past-performance warnings) must be present and is not evidence of impersonal advice.

sufficiency.ifEvidenceAbsent: Where personalised claims cite preferences that appear nowhere in the file, treat as unsupported personalisation.

queryGroups.requirement: Alternatives considered and reasons for rejection

queries.text: options considered leave existing plan switch funds internally set up a new plan
I do not recommend this option because reasons for rejection
alternative solutions stakeholder pension considered but not recommended
investment pathways considered and why they are not appropriate for you
comparison of alternative products and providers considered during research
do nothing option leaving things as they are was considered

falsePositiveGuards: Options listed without individual rejection reasons are a partial answer — the check asks for reasons, not just the list.
An alternative rejected in the research file but never mentioned in the report is a report gap, not a research gap.

sufficiency.ifAssertionAbsent: Potential Concern: no alternatives presented to the client.
sufficiency.ifEvidenceAbsent: Where the report claims options were assessed but no research document exists, treat the claim as unsupported.

queryGroups.requirement: Every existing arrangement has a stated recommended outcome and a rationale supporting it

queries.text: I recommend that you retain leave or transfer your existing plan with because
existing plan provider policy number and current value
review of existing arrangements and the recommended action for each

falsePositiveGuards: An arrangement appearing only in a valuation table has still been identified and needs a stated outcome; silence about it is the finding.
'No action required' is a recommended outcome, provided a reason is given for it.
A plan the client asked to leave alone still needs the instruction recorded; the client's wish is the rationale, not a substitute for one.

sufficiency.ifAssertionAbsent: Potential Concern: an existing arrangement is left with no recommended outcome.
sufficiency.ifEvidenceAbsent: Note as a gap; no existing arrangements were found to test the report's coverage against.
sufficiency.ifBothAbsent: No issue on this requirement; the client holds nothing existing.

queryGroups.requirement: Where a change is suggested, the report states whether it is recommended, who will implement it, and the intended outcome

queries.text: I recommend that you and I will arrange this on your behalf
the intended outcome of this change is to
agreed next steps and who will action them

falsePositiveGuards: 'You may wish to consider' is not a recommendation. A report using only that wording has not stated whether the adviser recommends the change.
An implementation step handled by the provider rather than the adviser is still a stated step; the finding is silence, not who happens to act.
A change the client instructed and the adviser is merely executing should say so; an execution-only instruction is not an absent recommendation.

sufficiency.ifAssertionAbsent: Potential Concern: a change is described with no statement of whether it is recommended or who will carry it out.
sufficiency.ifEvidenceAbsent: Assess on the report alone; the statement is the report's duty regardless of what the file holds.

queryGroups.requirement: Recommendations that present multiple possible outcomes without stating which is recommended and why

queries.text: you could either or alternatively you may wish to consider
the options available to you are set out below for you to choose
options discussed with the client and the option the client chose

falsePositiveGuards: Setting out options and then naming one as recommended is good practice, not a finding. The finding is an option left unresolved.
A client decision recorded in a file note resolves an option the report left open — check the notes before reporting it.
An option presented for information about a future decision (for example, how to take benefits later) is not an unresolved recommendation.

sufficiency.ifAssertionAbsent: No issue on this requirement; no open options were presented.
sufficiency.ifEvidenceAbsent: Potential Concern where the report leaves an option open and nothing in the file resolves it.

queryGroups.requirement: Recommendations state what action will be taken, when, and by whom where that is material to suitability

queries.text: the following will happen once you have signed and returned the application forms
timescales for the transfer and when your funds will be invested
implementation steps and expected timescales

falsePositiveGuards: Timing is material where the client is out of the market or working to a deadline; absent timing on a routine top-up is not a finding.
A timescale quoted as a provider service standard is a stated timescale.
Naming the adviser firm rather than an individual satisfies 'by whom'.

sufficiency.ifAssertionAbsent: Note as a gap; raise it as a concern only where timing or responsibility bears on suitability.

decision.noIssue: Evidence complete, consistent and supports the outcome. Each discrete recommendation carries its own client-specific rationale naming an objective; product, provider, wrapper and investment choices are justified; and alternatives are presented with reasons for rejection, corroborated by research.
decision.potentialConcern: Material clarification or additional evidence required. Rationale is boilerplate or shared verbatim across different recommendations, a recommendation names no objective, provider or wrapper choice is asserted without comparison, or alternatives are absent or listed without reasons.
decision.notApplicable: Trigger absent. No recommendation is made in the case.
severityHints: Highest: a recommendation with no rationale at all, or rationale that contradicts the case facts (e.g. 'lower costs' where the charge comparison shows an increase).
High: no alternatives considered on a case where research shows options were compared.
Moderate: rationale present but wholly generic across all recommendations.
Low: an alternative listed with a brief rather than reasoned rejection.
decision.overlayInstruction: Vulnerability overlay: consider whether any actual or potential drivers or characteristics of vulnerability, support needs, communication requirements or reasonable adjustments identified in the evidence materially affect this check's assessment or the conclusions it reaches. Where they do, say so in the finding. A vulnerability recorded in the file that has no bearing on this requirement is not itself a concern here — CHK-010 assesses vulnerability in its own right.
